Tiny Number Simon is a Simon-style digital memory game implemented in Wokwi. It uses eight active-high buttons as number inputs and a common-cathode 7-segment display to show the sequence and score. The game requires a slow or manually stepped clock and an active-low reset, with no microcontroller or external memory needed. The design is notable for its simple state-machine implementation and clear test procedure.

This project is a test design for a segment display, with minimal documentation stating 'this is just test'. It has eight input pins and eight output pins, but no functional description or test procedure. No external hardware is required. The design is not aimed at specific criteria and appears to be a placeholder.

This design implements a lightweight xoroshiro64+ random number generator with ring oscillator noise injection to provide entropy. It maintains two 32-bit states, generates a 32-bit random word per enabled clock cycle, and serializes it out with a valid pulse. The design can be seeded through an 8-bit interface and requires an external 1-bit ring oscillator noise source. It is notable for combining a PRNG with true randomness from an RO.

This is a minimal 4-bit accumulator-driven CPU implemented in Verilog. It fetches instructions from an internal ROM, decodes them, and performs ALU operations (ADD, SUB, AND, OR) on the accumulator with an immediate value. The design has eight input pins for data and opcode, and eight output pins for data and ALU results. It is intended as an educational example of a simple CPU architecture.

This ASIC implements a 60 Hz grid-forming reference using a CORDIC-locked sine wave generator and a linear dump-load controller for micro-inverters. It includes PWM modulators for driving an H-bridge and dump FET, with ADC sampling for AC and DC voltage feedback. The design requires substantial external hardware including a grid-tied solar system, H-bridge, transformer, rectifier, and dump load. It is notable for its complex control loops and power electronics application.

Triad01 is a clocked failsafe arbitration block for autonomous drone control paths, evaluating RC and FC health signals to select PRIMARY, FALLBACK, or SAFE_HOLD. It drives a 50 Hz PWM output and includes a scan chain for counter observability and lightweight LBIST for post-silicon diagnosis. The design supports four operating modes: normal, PWM-test, scan, and LBIST. It is notable for its built-in test features and safety-critical application.
